profile.address: Avenida de la Industria, 15, 28108 Alcobendas, Madrid, Spain
profile.reading:
DC01 is the original data center building on DATA4's MAD01 campus in Alcobendas, on the northern edge of Madrid, Spain, at Avenida de la Industria 15. DATA4 is a French headquartered data center developer and operator, founded in 2006 and based in Paris, led by chief executive Olivier Micheli since November 2014. The company designs, builds, finances, and operates its own facilities rather than developing for third party landlords, and its Madrid MAD01 campus is positioned toward colocation customers, cloud providers, and carriers, distinct from the newer, more hyperscale oriented MAD02 campus the company is separately building at San Agustín del Guadalix north of the city.

A 2023 trade press account of DC03 breaking ground, sourced to the operator, described DC01 as the campus's original and largest building, at 14 megawatts of IT capacity across 6,500 square meters, about 69,965 square feet, of white space. That same account put the two later buildings, DC02 and DC03, at 6.6 megawatts of IT capacity apiece across 3,000 square meters each, and described the finished MAD01 campus, at full build out, as an eight hectare site hosting six buildings totaling 70 megawatts. DATA4's own current Madrid landing page, by contrast, describes MAD01 as a single 50 megawatt campus across 4 hectares, a smaller figure that likely reflects capacity commissioned to date rather than the six building design end state described in 2023. This registry records both figures with attribution rather than resolving the gap between them. DC01 is reported by the operator to have come online in 2020, making it the founding building of the campus, several years before DC02 and DC03 followed.

DATA4's corporate ownership has changed twice since DC01 opened. AXA Investment Managers Alternatives sold DATA4 to Brookfield Infrastructure in a deal worth 2.4 billion dollars, agreed in April 2023 and completed that August. Then, in August 2025, Brookfield brought in Arjun Infrastructure Partners and Interogo Holding as new shareholders in a stake sale covering DATA4's stabilised hyperscale portfolio in Paris, Milan, and Madrid, a combined 244 megawatts of contracted capacity that a Brookfield SEC filing valued at 3.6 billion dollars. Brookfield kept a stake alongside the new investors, and DATA4's own management team, still led by Micheli, continues to run the business day to day. Because the August 2025 release names Madrid generally rather than MAD01 specifically, it is not possible to say from that document alone whether DC01, as the campus's oldest and largest building, sits inside the divested stabilised pool or is treated separately from it.

No tenant name for DC01 was found in any operator or trade source reviewed. No standby generator rating, utility interconnection figure, or onsite generation figure specific to this building was found either, only the campus level IT capacity figure of 14 megawatts already described above, which this registry attributes to DC01 specifically because the 2023 trade press account named it as an IT capacity figure for that building by name, distinguishing it from the campus wide totals that mix marketing and design figures.

profile.research_note: [session addition 2026-09-06] Replaced prior baxtel.com sourced content, baxtel is a banned aggregator directory under house rules and had to be dropped as a citation. Reconfirmed DC01's 14 MW / 6,500 sqm figure directly against the Data Center Dynamics DC03 groundbreaking article (English version), which is the same source already anchoring the sibling DC03 row (osm:way/301156874) in this registry. Set campus_power_note and campus_buildings_total (6) to match DC03's already established campus level facts verbatim, per instruction to keep MAD01's buildings internally consistent as a set. Added it_capacity_mw (14) and building_sqft (69965, converted from 6,500 sqm) as building specific figures because the DCD article names DC01 individually rather than only giving a campus total. DC01's reported 2020 opening year was retained from the prior record; this session did not find an independent primary source restating that exact year, so it is carried forward as a previously reported fact rather than freshly verified. No utility, standby generation, or onsite generation figure was found for this building.
profile.campus_power_note: The four power numbers for DATA4's MAD01 campus need to stay separate because two different totals are in circulation. DATA4's own current Madrid page states the MAD01 campus is 50 megawatts across 4 hectares. A 2023 trade press account of DC03's groundbreaking, sourced to the operator, instead describes an eight hectare site designed for six buildings totaling 70 megawatts once fully built, with DC01 at 14 MW IT capacity, DC02 at 6.6 MW IT capacity, and DC03 at 6.6 MW IT capacity confirmed individually. Both totals describe IT capacity, not utility interconnection ratings, standby generator ratings, or onsite generation figures, none of which were found published for this campus. This registry treats the 50 MW / 4 ha figure as the operator's current simplified marketing number and the 70 MW / six building / 8 ha figure as the more detailed design end state, and records both here rather than picking one.
